Two major things are lacking here:
- an explanation for the need of feeding the thing
- mention of the Foundation actually checking whether the thing can infest anything other.

I mean, they already determined that it's not the carpet but the fungus or whatever so it seems logical that it CAN spread but it seems strange and neglectful on their part that they didn't check: how does it do that, how fast, on what materials? Those are serious security-related issues and I think they deserve at least a small mention.

The Object Classes guide states, "Safe-class objects are those anomalies that are either sufficiently understood that they are now completely and reliably contained on a permanent basis or otherwise do not trigger their anomalous effects unless intentionally activated."

If the containment is reliable, I guess that effectively makes it "easy" as opposed to "difficult" in terms of keeping the thing locked up. The degrees of "easy" can be argued over for awhile depending on resource allocation.

But I don't think it's that big of a deal in this case. Let the author decide here.

item.content:encoded:
It seems unresolved, as it keeps coming up.

What do you suppose the purpose of object classes is?

I think they should be a way to categorize containment, in a way that allows for prioritization of resources and strategic planning. If you are, for example, forced to abandon a facility then you know that you absolutely must take (or neutralize) the Keter objects, should probably take the Euclid objects, but can leave the Safe objects in place. Unless you have some Safe objects that require maintainence, of course.

What's the purpose of muddling the classes?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, I like the test logs, except it should be animals -> humans -> oh hey, "observer effect" thing noticed, let's try it with multiple animals… nope, didn't do anything.

And the notes should be removed, as well as the time to drain the blood has no purpose being redacted, especially if we're supposed to see that it's getting faster. "Oh, it's a single digit of minutes, now it's another single digit of minutes!" Is it going from 9 to 8? 8 go 3? The rate of increase there could actually be scientifically important, but we don't get to see it.

I don't mind the comment on the color of the carpet, but it could be worded better. Kinda clunky the way it is now.

Overall, I like it, but these issues keep it from a +1. The concept being good keeps it from a -1.

E: The last note actually seems alright after looking again, though the wording could maybe be just a little better. The other two notes were written by Captain Obvious, so should definitely just be removed.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This is up for review. Come give it a look, eh?

This one just has not aged well. Well, first, here's what I like:

  • Fungus angle is kind of cool
  • I like the name

Here's what I don't like:

  • Horrid tone
  • Extremely trite in how it tells the effect, it couldn't be more straightforward if it tried.
  • lolFoundation
  • Test log is badly written and doesn't know how to pace itself.
  • This sentence: "Furthermore, the red coloring of the carpet is simply just that: the color of the carpet, having nothing to do with the organism or the task it performs. Theoretically, SCP-522 could live in a carpet of any color, undetected to the naked eye." which is completely pointless.
  • This is basically like that far side comic where the carpet ate people.

I don't know if there's much potential in "a carpet what eats people" but I hope someone finds something salvageable in here to write a cool article about.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Plus there's the fact that it makes it blatantly obvious that it was written by someone after they'd established everything that goes in the main article. If it were done properly, most things in the experiment log would happen BEFORE the main report gets written; in this case, animal testing would have been one of the first things they did.

item.title: Re: Determination
item.content:encoded:
I wonder… if we were to attach a person to the wall of the chamber in a position to see the carpet doing its thing and put something on the center of the carpet, would it act in the same way? What would happen if the thing placed on the carpet was dead? Or what if it had no blood at all, at least not red blood? I'm interested in what would happen if you introduced it to other SCPs, too.

Overall, it's really great and I do not want to find myself walking across the carpet only to find that it's possessed by something that will kill me in a horrible horrible fashion.

item.title: Re: Determination
item.content:encoded:
Holy cow someone commented on mine! Sorry I didn't reply until now!

Could be tested! I included that to, well, suggest that it had some amount of intelligence, and to make it harder to detect if a given carpet was, in fact, a host to the organism. Because if it 'acted' when another could see it happening, the victim would be freed and the carpet likely destroyed….

item.title: Determination
item.content:encoded: I am wondering something: Would the research team ever consider that it might not be a matter of 'observers' but of 'potentially reachable victims'? A rat off to the side is relatively quite close, as it takes far less carpet to engulf. Whereas a person pretty much has to be in the center. Would / could we test that?
